newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian court orders opposition chiefs' release.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian court orders opposition chiefs' release.

text.p: A Nigerian court on Friday ordered the police to release three veteran opposition figures from an investigation into the murder of the wife of detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola.
Judge Abdul Kafarati told the Lagos court that the arrest and detention of the three was unlawful, in spite of a police appeal that they should still be held.

Abraham Adesanya, Ayo Adebanjo and Ganiyu Dawodu, all prominent figures in the opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), have been detained since June to help the police inquiry into the murder of Kudirat Abiola.
She was shot in the head while driving along a Lagos street.
The court initially ruled the detention of the three men unlawful but the police appealed against the court ruling.
Abiola's vocal wife had led the campaign to free him and install him as president in line with the results of a 1993 election, annulled by a former military government.
NADECO has also been campaigning for the military rulers to release Abiola, detained since 1994 when he declared himself president in defiance of the military rulers.
